title: Bats
objective: After this level you can explain how bats fly and find food with echolocation.
summary: More than 1,300 bat species make up about one-fifth of mammal species. Bats are the only true flying mammals, on hand-shaped wings, and many hunt by echolocation.

cards.headline: About 1 in 5 mammal species is a bat.
cards.body: The U.S. Geological Survey counts more than 1,300 bat species. Pick five mammal species at random and, on average, one of them is a bat. Two tricks set bats apart: they fly, and many of them see with sound.

cards.headline: A wing made from a hand
cards.body: Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight. The wing is a modified hand: a thin, flexible skin stretched between long finger bones. Spread your fingers and imagine the skin between them larger, thinner and stretched wide. That's a bat wing, and the order's name, Chiroptera, means 'hand wing.'

cards.headline: Seeing with sound
cards.body: In echolocation, a bat sends out calls that bounce off objects and come back to its ears. The echoes tell the bat what's out there. Most of those calls are ultrasound, too high-pitched for you to hear. After dark, the air above you may be full of bat shouts you'll never notice.

mascot.line: Loudest party in town, and you're not on the frequency list.

cards.fact: Closing in, a bat speeds up its calls.
cards.context: When a bat detects an insect it wants to eat, it fires off a rapid series of calls to pinpoint exactly where the prey is. More calls mean fresher echoes, the way you'd glance more often at something you were about to catch.

questions.prompt: What is a bat's wing built from?

options.label: Feathers along the arm
options.rationale: Bats have no feathers; the wing is skin.

options.label: A modified hand with skin stretched between long fingers
A stiff flap of skin along the ribs only
options.rationale: The skin stretches between finger bones.

options.label: Hardened scales
options.rationale: Bat wings are thin, flexible skin.

questions.explanation: A bat's wing is a modified hand: flexible skin stretched between long finger bones.

questions.prompt: How does echolocation tell a bat where things are?

options.label: It sees heat given off by prey
It feels vibrations through its feet
options.rationale: The bat is listening, not feeling.

options.label: Its calls bounce back as echoes

questions.explanation: Bats send out calls, mostly ultrasound, and listen to the echoes that return from objects and prey.

questions.prompt: Level 11 counted about 6,800 living mammal species. How many of them are bats?

options.label: About 3,400
options.rationale: That would be half of all mammals.
